english.title: Tampering with the National Identity Register - Identity Cards Act 2006
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) engaged in conduct, namely **(..SPECIFY THE CONDUCT..), that caused an unauthorised modification of information recorded in the National Identity Register, and at the time of that conduct you intended to, or were reckless as to whether or not your conduct would, cause such a modification

english.notes:
(i) For the current legislation, please see the Identity Documents Act 2010.
(ii) Section 29(3) of the Identity Cards Act 2006 provides that cases in which conduct causes a modification of information recorded in the Register include -
(a) where it contributes to a modification of such information; and (b) where it makes it more difficult or impossible for such information to be retrieved in a legible form from a computer on which it is stored by the Secretary of State, or contributes to making that more difficult or impossible.
(iii) Section 29(4) of the Identity Cards Act 2006 provides that it is immaterial -
(a) whether the conduct constituting the offence, or any of it, took place in the United Kingdom; or
(b) in the case of conduct outside the United Kingdom, whether it is the conduct of a British citizen.
(iv) Section 29(5) of the Identity Cards Act 2006 provides that a modification is unauthorised, in relation to the person whose conduct causes it, if -
(a) he is not himself entitled to determine if the modification may be made; and (b) he does not have a consent to the modification from a person who is so entitled.
(v) Section 29(6) of the Identity Cards Act 2006 provides a defence.
(vi) Section 29(8) of the Identity Cards Act 2006 provides that in respect of conduct wholly or partly outside the United Kingdom -
(a) proceedings for the offence may be taken at any place in the United Kingdom; and (b) the offence may for all incidental purposes be treated as having been committed at any such place.
(vii) Section 29(9) of the Identity Cards Act 2006 provides that conduct includes acts and omissions; and modification includes temporary modification.

other.penalty:
SUMMARY: Twelve months imprisonment and/or fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.

In relation to an offence committed before the commencement of section 154(1) of the Criminal Justice Act 2003 the penalty is six months imprisonment and/or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.

INDICTMENT: Ten years imprisonment and/or fine.Time limit for prosecutions:
